key_insight: Bregman ADMM can be shown to avoid strict-saddle KKT points almost surely under two-sided relative smoothness, yielding second-order stationary limits in nonconvex, non-Lipschitz problems.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical convergence guarantee for matrix/tensor and distributed optimization problems where standard Lipschitz-gradient assumptions fail.
method: Model the problem with a Bregman kernel and two-sided relative smoothness instead of global gradient Lipschitzness.
Prove the Bregman ADMM iteration is a smooth primal-dual fixed-point map on an invariant open state space.
Show strict-saddle KKT points are unstable fixed points, so random initialization converges to them with probability zero.
evidence_signal: The paper validates the theory with numerical experiments on distributed matrix factorization and a symmetric tensor factorization example.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on specific structural assumptions and invariant-domain conditions, so implementation must preserve the required Bregman geometry and block structure.
paper_title: Second-Order KKT Guarantees for Bregman ADMM in Nonconvex and Non-Lipschitz Optimization
